name: Sirmauri
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Hendriksen, Hans. 1986. Himachali Studies III: Grammar. Copenhagen: Munksgaard.
earlier_scan.note: Full grammar of Himachali covering Sirmauri exists (also Grierson LSI IX.IV specimens); not found online.

sources.citation: Hendriksen, Hans. 1976. Himachali Studies I: Vocabulary. Copenhagen: Munksgaard (Det Kongelige Danske Videnskabernes Selskab, Hist.-filos. Meddelelser 48:1).
sources.note: Not about Sirmauri: a Kotgarhi/Koci vocabulary that cites LSI Sirmauri forms in passing (e.g. 'LSI p. 477 (Sirmauri) gas'). Its tone-accent notation concerns Kotgarhi. Glottolog's sole descriptive reference for sirm1239, Himachali Studies III: Grammar (1986), has lgcode 'Kotgarhi = Pahari-Mahasu [bfz], Koci = Pahari-Mahasu [bfz]' in Glottolog's own BibTeX, so it is a Mahasu Pahari grammar, not a Sirmauri one; vol. III not located online.

sources.citation: Bailey, T. Grahame. 1908. The Languages of the Northern Himalayas, being Studies in the Grammar of Twenty-six Himalayan Dialects. London: RAS. / Bailey, T. Grahame. 1920. Linguistic Studies from the Himalayas. London: RAS.
sources.note: Neither describes Sirmauri; 1908 p. iii mentions only that 104,000 persons in Nahan (Sirmaur) were returned as speaking Sirmauri, 'a dialect which will be found to have considerable affinity to the dialects specially dealt with'.

sources.citation: Pandey, Anshuman & Biswajit Mandal. 2025. Proposal to encode Sirmauri in Unicode (L2/25-134). Unicode Technical Committee.
sources.note: Nothing; script proposal. Its reference list cites no linguistic description of Sirmauri other than Grierson 1916, confirming the thinness of the literature.

sources.citation: Vedamanickam, P. Edward & Jhuma Ghosh. [2023]. "Sirmauri". In Language Division, Office of the Registrar General, India (ed.), Linguistic Survey of India: Himachal Pradesh, Chapter 2 (Indo-Aryan languages: Hindi language / mother tongues), pp. 615-669 (PDF pp. 636-690). Based on Mother Tongue Survey of India fieldwork, Sirmaur district, 2014.
sources.note: Nothing. Phonology (pp. 618-633) gives 10 vowels + 33 consonants, then "Suprasegmental Phonemes" (pp. 619-620, PDF 640-641) covering only (a) Length: "Length is not phonemic here" and (b) Nasalization: "No minimal pair could be formed to establish nasalization as phonemic in Sirmauri." No stress, accent, tone or intonation subsection; the word "stress" occurs once, in the generic definition of a syllable (p. 631). Verified on the rendered page images, not just scanned.

sources.citation: Sharma, J. C. 2002. An Introduction to Sirmauri: Grammatical Gender. Language in India 1(9), January 2002.
sources.note: Nothing; morphology of gender in the Giripari variety (Shilai and Sangrah tehsils) only. Cited by the LSI-HP chapter as the only other linguistic work on Sirmauri.

sources.citation: Grierson, George A. 1916. Linguistic Survey of India, Vol. IX Part IV: Specimens of the Pahari Languages and Gujuri. Calcutta: Superintendent of Government Printing. Sirmauri section pp. 456-489 (Dharthi pp. 458-477, Giripari pp. 478-489).
sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent. The Giripari "II. Pronunciation" paragraph (p. 478) treats only vowel quality/spelling variation (a ~ o, a ~ o, short e), explicitly based on written specimens. p. 457: "Nothing of consequence has hitherto been written concerning Sirmauri, nor... does it possess any literature." The only accent remarks in the volume concern other languages (Bhadrawahi/Bhalesi, Khowar).

sources.citation: Office of the Registrar General, India, Language Division. Mother Tongue Survey of India (MTSI) report on Sirmauri (fieldwork Sirmaur district, 2014), the underlying survey report from which the LSI-HP chapter was written.
sources.tag: wanted: likely states stress, not held
sources.note: Same fieldwork as the LSI-HP chapter; a fuller MTSI report might carry a suprasegmental section beyond length and nasalization, though the published chapter suggests stress was not treated. Existence as a separate published document not confirmed by any record I saw; the chapter only says the language 'has been surveyed under Mother Tongue Survey of India (MTSI) Project... in 2014'.

sources.note: Glottolog's only descriptive reference for sirm1239, and the source named by the earlier scan, but Glottolog's own record codes it to Kotgarhi and Koci (Mahasu Pahari, maha1287); it would give Kotgarhi/Koci accent facts, not Sirmauri ones. Listed so the misassignment is on record; Harvard holds the series in print (Widener LSoc 1261.8 vol. 48).
